verdict.rationale: OpenCode supplies the building blocks for background automation rather than a dedicated automation feature. It runs tasks in a GitHub Actions runner when triggered by a comment, working in a new branch and opening a PR. It also offers non-interactive `opencode run`, `--auto` permission approval, a headless `opencode serve` server, and an SDK for programmatic control. Any scheduling or triggering beyond GitHub comments must be wired up by the user, and one community report says the agent sometimes gets stuck in long or nested sessions. missing for 10: native scheduled/recurring automations, a first-party background task manager or monitoring UI, independent hands-on corroboration of reliable unattended runs.
